title: Workload-driven batch policy suggester and safe rollout
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a workload-driven suggestion engine that profiles live and historical request streams and proposes batching + caching configs with predicted cost and latency impact. The feature must provide human-readable heuristics, numeric estimates, and a safe automated apply/rollback plan that respects latency SLOs and GPU utilization limits. We will support continuous batching parameters (min_batch, max_batch, batch_timeout_ms, token_aware_threshold) and cache policies (kv_prefix_ttl, prefix_hwm) and expose a confidence score for each recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: Engine produces a ranked list of batch+cache config suggestions per service with estimated cost delta and P95 latency delta
Suggestion includes a confidence score and which workload fingerprints influenced the recommendation
Automated canary apply: 1% traffic for 30m with automatic promotion to 10%/50%/100% when thresholds met
Rollback triggers implemented: P95 latency increase > 20% or CPU/GPU saturation > 85% or error rate increase > 0.5%
CI/e2e validation harness runs a synthetic workload test against suggested configs and validates basic correctness
Operational dashboard (Grafana) shows before/after cost per token, batch size distribution, and kv-cache hit-rate
work_notes: 2026-02-10 Aisha K: Kickoff - scoped MVP to suggestions + safe apply automation for Hosted API routes. Decided to prioritize interpretability over a black-box ML model for initial rollout.
2026-02-12 Marco L: Spike results - profiled 48h of traffic from two sample tenants. Observed bimodal seq-len distribution; token-aware batching yields most benefit on mixed short/long workloads.
2026-02-15 Design review with Sofia M: UX needs to show predicted cost savings and clear rollback action. Added requirement for a 'why this suggestion' rationale string for each recommendation.

2026-02-17 Engineering decision: hybrid approach - heuristics (moving-window percentiles + exponential smoothing) to fingerprint workload; small ML regressor (lightweight XGBoost) to predict cost delta when enough historical data exists. Heuristic fallbacks for cold-start tenants.

2026-02-19 Implementation note: Added token_sensitivity_score and batch_timeout_safety bound to prevent unbounded latency increases on spikes. Default safe bounds: max_batch <= 1024 tokens or hardware-constrained limit, batch_timeout_ms <= 50ms for P95-sensitive routes.
2026-02-21 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4952 - initial suggester + unit tests. Integration tests are mocked; need to hook e2e harness.
2026-02-22 Telemetry plan: Dashboard panels in Grafana (cost-per-token, avg batch size, kv-cache hit-rate, P95 latency, GPU utilization). Alert rules defined for canary rollouts.

2026-02-24 Safety playbook drafted: canary windows, rollback conditions, manual abort flow, and post-rollback incident report template. Stored in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Batch+Suggester+Playbook
2026-02-26 Load test job: added synthetic driver (k6-based) to run 30m profiles for suggested configs. Sample job: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/actions/runs/7890123
2026-02-27 QA notes: edge case - DRY runs where kv-cache hit-rate is artificially high in staging produce optimistic savings. Added a staging gating rule to normalize cache state before evaluation.

2026-02-28 Marco L: Rolling apply MVP ready behind feature flag. Canary automation prepared; will run on 2 internal tenants first next week. Follow-up tasks: instrument rollback latency spike tracing and add an explicit operator approval path.
